rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (sensors at +/-3 cm, 16 mm footprints, kp 2.25, kd 0.9, base 1.2, mass 0.6, body 0.14) is the best design so far at 893.6. Oval finishes 20/20 at 2.04 s, s-bend 20/20 at 2.25 s, and slalom 15/20, with 5 off-track ends and 0.25 line-loss events per run. Slalom steering oscillation is low (0.25) and rms error is 0.012 m, so the loop is not jittering. The slalom failures are off-track exits after a loss or overshoot on sharp bends. Iteration 4 (base 1.1) got worse on the slalom, so speed is not the cause. Iteration 5 (sensors widened to +/-4 cm, kp 3.0, kd 1.2) scored 887.7, slightly below iteration 3, and its slalom had 14/20 finishes with more control effort (8.0), so widening the spread did not help. Change: keep the iteration 3 geometry and base_speed 1.2, and raise kd from 0.9 to 1.2 with kp held at 2.25. The aim is more damping on the sharp slalom bends where overshoot carries the robot off the tape. Steering oscillation (0.25) leaves room for more derivative action, and the oval and s-bend should be mostly unaffected. Expected result: slalom finish rate of 0.8 or higher and a slalom mean above 800, with oval and s-bend close to iteration 3. Hypotheses: (H1) the failures are overshoot, so kd 1.2 cuts off-track ends without raising oscillation above about 0.3; (H2) if slalom off-track ends persist with low line loss, the cause is kp too high for the tightest bends, and the next step is kp 2.0; (H3) if line_loss_events rise, the 16 mm footprint at 3 cm is the limit, and the next step is 12 mm sensors. Measurements wanted per track: completion, completion_time, progress, line_loss_events, max_error, steering_oscillation, control_effort, and noise_robustness, to separate line loss from overshoot.
